title: Comparison of imaging based single-cell resolution spatial transcriptomics profiling platforms using formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumor samples
concrete_content: Compares CosMx, MERFISH and uni- or multimodal Xenium on serial FFPE lung adenocarcinoma and mesothelioma TMA sections against bulk RNA-seq, multiplex immunofluorescence, GeoMx, H&E and manual pathology phenotyping.
decision_changed: Makes sample format, probe design, segmentation and pathology usability part of platform selection rather than selecting by advertised resolution alone.
constraints: Serial sections are not same-cell truth; only two tumour types, TMA format and time-specific product versions were tested.
skill_action: Build a platform-version passport; match platform to tissue, panel and estimand; require orthogonal concordance and manual pathology review.
writing_requirement: Methods: platform, chemistry, panel, section order and references; Results: matched performance and failure modes; Figure legend: platform and serial-section identity; Discussion: tissue and version limits.

title: Systematic benchmarking of high-throughput subcellular spatial transcriptomics platforms across human tumors
concrete_content: Profiles serial colon, liver and ovarian tumour sections with Stereo-seq v1.3, Visium HD FFPE, CosMx 6K and Xenium 5K, with CODEX, same-sample scRNA-seq and manual nuclear annotation as orthogonal references.
decision_changed: Requires platform comparison to cover sensitivity, specificity, diffusion, segmentation, annotation and spatial clustering with matched biological material.
constraints: Gene panels, chemistry and software differ; adjacent sections do not provide cell-by-cell ground truth and the tumour set is limited.
skill_action: Select platforms against the full assay contract; record panel and software versions; report metric-specific trade-offs rather than one winner.
writing_requirement: Methods: serial-section allocation and all reference assays; Results: metric-by-platform comparison; Figure legend: section and platform; Discussion: panel, tissue and adjacency limits.

title: Systematic benchmarking of imaging spatial transcriptomics platforms in FFPE tissues
concrete_content: Benchmarks Xenium, MERSCOPE and CosMx on serial FFPE TMAs containing 17 tumour and 16 normal tissue types, comparing matched-gene counts, specificity, cell typing, subclustering and segmentation errors.
decision_changed: Makes FFPE tissue breadth, matched genes, false discovery and segmentation error explicit platform-choice criteria.
constraints: TMA cores do not represent whole sections; results are platform-version and panel specific and do not cover sequencing-based assays.
skill_action: Use tissue- and panel-matched benchmarks; preserve full-section morphology checks; avoid extrapolating a global platform rank.
writing_requirement: Methods: TMA design, matched gene universe and segmentation; Results: sensitivity, specificity and FDR; Figure legend: tissue, panel and platform; Discussion: TMA and product-version limits.

title: Standardized metrics for assessment and reproducibility of imaging-based spatial transcriptomics datasets
concrete_content: Creates the multisite Spatial Touchstone dataset across six tissues and introduces STSOPs and SpatialQM for sensitivity, dynamic range, signal-to-noise, FDR, annotation and cross-site reproducibility.
decision_changed: Requires prespecified, reproducible technical metrics and cross-site controls before biological interpretation of imaging spatial data.
constraints: Core evaluation centres on Xenium and CosMx; technical reproducibility does not establish biological validity for a new panel or tissue.
skill_action: Adopt a spatial QC passport with positive and negative controls; compare against touchstones; separate technical PASS from biological interpretation.
writing_requirement: Methods: SOP, sites, controls and metrics; Results: cross-site reproducibility with uncertainty; Figure legend: site, tissue and platform; Discussion: platform coverage and biological-validity boundary.

title: FICTURE: scalable segmentation-free analysis of submicron-resolution spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Uses a multilayer Dirichlet factor model to infer pixel-level spatial factors from billions of submicron transcript coordinates across sequencing- and imaging-based platforms.
decision_changed: Creates a segmentation-free route for irregular, fibrotic, vascular, muscular or lipid-rich regions where cell boundaries are unreliable.
constraints: Factors are not cells; factor number, mixed pixels and biological labels remain model dependent.
skill_action: Use segmentation-free analysis as a sensitivity path; annotate factors with orthogonal morphology and markers; never call factors observed cell types.
writing_requirement: Methods: binning, factor count and priors; Results: factor stability and orthogonal support; Figure legend: inferred factor versus cell; Discussion: non-cellular and model-dependent boundary.

title: SpotSweeper: spatially aware quality control for spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Uses local spatial neighbourhoods to distinguish local outliers and regional artifacts, including systematic low-quality barcodes, dryspots and hangnails.
decision_changed: Prevents direct reuse of dissociated scRNA-seq QC thresholds and makes local and regional artifact detection mandatory.
constraints: True rare biological regions can resemble artifacts; removal decisions depend on tissue morphology and replicated context.
skill_action: Run global and spatial QC; overlay flags on histology; preserve pre- and post-filter maps; require sensitivity analysis for removed regions.
writing_requirement: Methods: neighbourhood, thresholds and artifact rules; Results: flagged area and sensitivity; Figure legend: retained and removed spots; Discussion: possible removal of true spatial biology.

title: Cell simulation as cell segmentation
concrete_content: Introduces Proseg, a probabilistic cell-simulation segmentation method, and benchmarks it across MERSCOPE, CosMx and Xenium tumour datasets, including difficult tumour-infiltrating immune cells.
decision_changed: Makes segmentation algorithm choice and alternative-boundary sensitivity a prerequisite for cell-level state and neighbourhood claims.
constraints: Morphologically plausible boundaries are not cell-by-cell truth and demonstrations are tumour weighted.
skill_action: Compare at least two defensible segmentations or a segmentation-free path; quantify transcript reassignment and downstream stability.
writing_requirement: Methods: image channels, segmentation model and alternatives; Results: boundary and downstream stability; Figure legend: boundary source; Discussion: absence of definitive cell truth.

title: Impact and correction of segmentation errors in spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Reanalysis across tissues and platforms shows misassigned molecules can dominate differential expression, neighbour influence and ligand-receptor findings; local matrix factorization reduces admixture.
decision_changed: Requires segmentation uncertainty to propagate into every cell-level downstream result instead of remaining a QC checkbox.
constraints: Correction reduces admixture but cannot restore lost molecules or establish the true originating cell.
skill_action: Audit molecule reassignment; repeat DE, neighbourhood and CCC after correction or alternative segmentation; downgrade unstable claims.
writing_requirement: Methods: segmentation and correction; Results: downstream before-after sensitivity; Figure legend: corrected status; Discussion: residual assignment uncertainty.

title: Accurate, scalable and cross-platform cell identification for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Cellist combines image and expression information for scalable cell segmentation and identification across Stereo-seq, Seq-Scope, seqFISH+, STARmap and Xenium.
decision_changed: Supports cross-platform multimodal cell assignment but still requires tissue-specific validation of within-cell coherence and annotations.
constraints: Performance depends on image quality, transcript density and morphology; tested-platform compatibility does not guarantee transfer to every tissue.
skill_action: Validate cell boundaries, within-cell transcriptomic coherence and cell-type calls; retain an unresolved label when evidence conflicts.
writing_requirement: Methods: image and expression inputs, model and versions; Results: coherence and annotation gains; Figure legend: inferred boundary and label; Discussion: new-tissue transfer limits.

title: Inferring histology-associated gene expression gradients in spatial transcriptomic studies
concrete_content: Spatial Gradient Screening detects supervised histology-associated expression patterns without prior clustering and contrasts them with conventional differential expression.
decision_changed: Adds a continuous, cluster-free gradient estimand when tissue structure is directional or graded.
constraints: Results depend on the chosen histological variable, coordinate and direction and show association rather than a driving mechanism.
skill_action: Predefine the histological axis; compare gradient and grouped analyses; assess rotation or coordinate sensitivity; validate with pathology.
writing_requirement: Methods: histology variable, coordinate and model; Results: gradient effect and uncertainty; Figure legend: axis and scale; Discussion: association and axis dependence.

title: A visual-omics foundation model to bridge histopathology with spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: OmiCLIP is trained on 2.2 million paired image-transcriptomic patches from 32 organs; Loki supports alignment, annotation, decomposition, retrieval and H&E-to-expression prediction.
decision_changed: Makes external tissue and staining validation mandatory and separates histology-predicted expression from measured spatial expression.
constraints: Domain shift, gene-rank sentence encoding, pretraining overlap and platform coverage can inflate performance; output is predicted.
skill_action: Audit corpus overlap and staining domain; compare simple image baselines; validate held-out measured sections; label predictions in every output.
writing_requirement: Methods: corpus, model, overlap and split; Results: held-out baseline-relative metrics; Figure legend: predicted versus measured; Discussion: domain shift and non-measurement.

title: SpaIM: single-cell spatial transcriptomics imputation via style transfer
concrete_content: Uses style-transfer integration of scRNA-seq and spatial data to impute unmeasured genes and reports comparisons across 53 datasets and 12 methods.
decision_changed: Requires held-out gene and dataset validation before imputed genes enter domain, differential expression or CCC analyses.
constraints: Reference shift and shared-content assumptions transfer scRNA biases; imputation cannot create direct spatial measurements.
skill_action: Hold out measured genes and samples; compare simple mapping baselines; keep an inferred layer; block unvalidated imputed-only biomarkers.
writing_requirement: Methods: reference, overlap, holdout and model; Results: measured-gene validation and calibration; Figure legend: measured or imputed; Discussion: reference and non-observation limits.

title: Interpretable spatially aware dimension reduction of spatial transcriptomics with STAMP
concrete_content: STAMP uses a deep generative topic model to return low-dimensional spatial topics and associated gene modules across single, multiple and time-series sections.
decision_changed: Promotes interpretable topic and gene-module reporting instead of treating an embedding or cluster as a biological entity.
constraints: Topic number, priors, batch structure and model fit change domains; topics are not observed cell types.
skill_action: Test topic-number and seed stability; connect modules to markers and morphology; retain continuous topic scores.
writing_requirement: Methods: topic model, priors and stability; Results: module support and sample consistency; Figure legend: topic is inferred; Discussion: model and annotation dependence.

title: Novae: a graph-based foundation model for spatial transcriptomics data
concrete_content: Trains a graph model on nearly 30 million cells across 18 tissues for zero-shot domain inference, batch handling and nested domain hierarchies across panels and technologies.
decision_changed: Requires task-level zero-shot validation and prevents naming a pretrained domain as a new cell type or mechanism without evidence.
constraints: Training tissue and panel coverage constrain transfer; rare or novel states may be absorbed into learned domains.
skill_action: Audit pretraining overlap and panel genes; compare non-pretrained spatial baselines; validate domains with pathology and markers.
writing_requirement: Methods: pretraining corpus, overlap and inference mode; Results: zero-shot baseline-relative performance; Figure legend: learned domain; Discussion: coverage and novelty limits.

title: Interpretable, flexible and spatially aware integration of multiple spatial transcriptomics datasets from diverse sources
concrete_content: INSPIRE combines adversarial graph learning with non-negative matrix factorization to integrate multiple technologies while returning spatial factors and gene programs.
decision_changed: Makes condition preservation and overcorrection audits mandatory for cross-sample and cross-platform integration.
constraints: Adversarial alignment can erase real condition or patient differences; performance is application and parameter dependent.
skill_action: Preserve sample covariates; compare unintegrated and integrated signals; use leave-one-sample-out checks; report factor stability.
writing_requirement: Methods: graph, covariates, adversarial objective and parameters; Results: mixing plus biological preservation; Figure legend: integrated state; Discussion: possible overcorrection.

title: STIE: Single-cell level deconvolution, convolution, and clustering in in situ capturing-based spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Aligns spot expression with histological nuclei using expectation maximization to deconvolve spots, recover cells from gap areas and cluster at whole-slide scale.
decision_changed: Requires recovered cells and cell-specific expression to be labelled as estimates and validated against true single-cell-resolution assays.
constraints: Nuclear detection errors, non-nucleated or multinucleated cells and histology-expression mismatch violate the reconstruction assumptions.
skill_action: Validate on matched high-resolution regions; quantify recovered-cell uncertainty; compare spot-level conclusions; block observation language.
writing_requirement: Methods: nuclei, alignment and EM assumptions; Results: reconstruction accuracy and sensitivity; Figure legend: observed nuclei versus reconstructed cells; Discussion: model-estimated cell boundary.

title: Ultra-precision deconvolution of spatial transcriptomics decodes immune heterogeneity and fate-defining programs in tissues
concrete_content: UCASpatial applies entropy-based weighting to map low-abundance and transcriptionally heterogeneous subpopulations and demonstrates applications in colorectal cancer and wound repair.
decision_changed: Raises the validation bar for rare-subpopulation deconvolution and links cell-fraction estimates to spatial communities only after benchmark support.
constraints: Reference quality and compositional identifiability constrain rare-state recovery; reported superiority and mechanisms require independent tissue validation.
skill_action: Audit reference match and rare-state detectability; perturb marker sets; compare coarse and fine labels; validate with in situ markers.
writing_requirement: Methods: reference, entropy weighting and benchmarks; Results: uncertainty and marker robustness; Figure legend: deconvolved estimate; Discussion: rare-state and external-validation limits.

title: Categorization of 34 computational methods to detect spatially variable genes from spatially resolved transcriptomics data
concrete_content: Classifies 34 SVG methods into overall SVG, cell-type-specific SVG and spatial-domain-marker SVG categories and compares their inferential targets and tests.
decision_changed: Forces the SVG estimand to be named before method selection and blocks cross-category performance or result comparisons.
constraints: It is a taxonomy review rather than a universal benchmark or consensus; the method landscape will evolve.
skill_action: Route by SVG category, resolution and null; record test and multiplicity; avoid a generic SVG claim.
writing_requirement: Methods: SVG category, null and test; Results: category-specific effects; Figure legend: target and resolution; Discussion: category and benchmark limits.

title: Statistical identification of cell type-specific spatially variable genes in spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Celina uses a spatially varying coefficient model for cell-type-specific SVG detection with type I error control in single-cell- and spot-resolution data.
decision_changed: Requires cell-type-specific spatial tests rather than conflating cell abundance with within-cell-type expression pattern.
constraints: Spot-resolution ct-SVGs depend on composition estimates and model assumptions; deconvolution error can create apparent variation.
skill_action: Report composition source and uncertainty; simulate or permute under the fitted design; validate priority genes by in situ assay.
writing_requirement: Methods: cell fractions, spatial model and multiplicity; Results: effect surfaces and error control; Figure legend: ct-SVG and resolution; Discussion: deconvolution dependence.

title: ELLA: modeling subcellular spatial variation of gene expression within cells in high-resolution spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: ELLA uses an over-dispersed nonhomogeneous Poisson process in a unified cell coordinate system to test nuclear, cytoplasmic and membrane-associated RNA localization.
decision_changed: Creates a distinct subcellular estimand and requires segmentation and cell-shape normalization audits before localization claims.
constraints: Boundary and coordinate errors directly affect localization; statistical association does not establish RNA transport or retention mechanism.
skill_action: Audit segmentation and transcript localization error; stratify by cell shape and cycle; validate selected RNAs by orthogonal imaging.
writing_requirement: Methods: cell coordinate, point process and segmentation; Results: localization effect and robustness; Figure legend: compartment and coordinate; Discussion: non-mechanistic localization boundary.

title: Mapping cellular interactions from spatially resolved transcriptomics data
concrete_content: Spacia uses multiple-instance learning to model multiple senders to one receiver without restricting inference to known ligand-receptor pairs and evaluates MERSCOPE, CosMx and Xenium data.
decision_changed: Expands CCC beyond nearest-neighbour ligand-receptor overlap while preserving its status as a statistical interaction hypothesis.
constraints: Predicted gene-to-gene effects are observational and depend on segmentation, distance and model assumptions.
skill_action: Use spatial nulls and negative controls; repeat under alternative boundaries; prioritize perturbable interactions; avoid causal verbs.
writing_requirement: Methods: sender-receiver definition, radius, null and model; Results: effect and stability; Figure legend: inferred interaction; Discussion: observational non-causality.

title: CytoSignal detects locations and dynamics of ligand-receptor signaling at cellular resolution from spatial transcriptomic data
concrete_content: CytoSignal maps contact-dependent and diffusible ligand-receptor scores, gradients, differential signaling and inferred temporal dynamics, with selected in situ proximity ligation validation.
decision_changed: Requires location-aware LR analysis and promotes orthogonal in situ validation before signaling claims are strengthened.
constraints: Temporal dynamics are model inferred and limited LR validation cannot establish every predicted interaction.
skill_action: Prespecify interaction range and LR database; use spatial nulls; validate high-priority pairs by proximity or perturbation.
writing_requirement: Methods: LR source, spatial kernel and validation; Results: effect, uncertainty and validated subset; Figure legend: inferred or validated; Discussion: limited causal and temporal support.

title: CellNEST reveals cell-cell relay networks using attention mechanisms on spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: CellNEST uses attention to infer ligand-receptor-ligand-receptor relay networks and provides cell-level interactive spatial visualization.
decision_changed: Adds relay-network hypotheses but requires them to be distinguished from direct pairwise signaling and experimentally tested.
constraints: Attention weights and relay paths are putative and depend on database, distance, segmentation and model architecture.
skill_action: Run database and radius sensitivity; test relay order against alternatives; select tractable nodes for perturbation or multiplex imaging.
writing_requirement: Methods: database, graph and attention model; Results: stable relays and controls; Figure legend: putative relay; Discussion: attention and causality boundary.

title: STAIG: Spatial transcriptomics analysis via image-aided graph contrastive learning for domain exploration and alignment-free integration
concrete_content: STAIG combines expression, coordinates and histology through graph contrastive learning for spatial-domain detection and multi-slice integration without prealignment.
decision_changed: Provides an alignment-free representation route while requiring separate physical registration for pathology or radiology co-localization claims.
constraints: Deep embeddings and batch removal can overcorrect biology; no-prealignment integration does not establish micron-scale coordinate correspondence.
skill_action: Compare image-free and simple graph baselines; audit condition preservation; perform explicit registration for local cross-modal claims.
writing_requirement: Methods: modalities, graph, contrastive objective and batches; Results: domain and preservation metrics; Figure legend: integrated versus registered; Discussion: embedding and registration boundary.

title: STORIES: learning cell fate landscapes from spatial transcriptomics using optimal transport
concrete_content: Extends optimal transport to learn a spatially informed differentiation potential from multiple measured time points and benchmarks three Stereo-seq spatiotemporal atlases.
decision_changed: Requires true time-series sampling before spatial trajectory inference and separates inferred drivers from lineage evidence.
constraints: Transport relies on continuity, cost and sampling assumptions; recovered paths and regulators are hypothesis generating.
skill_action: Record time points and destructive sampling; test cost and neighbourhood sensitivity; compare non-spatial OT; validate with lineage or perturbation.
writing_requirement: Methods: time points, transport cost and assumptions; Results: path uncertainty and known-marker recovery; Figure legend: inferred trajectory; Discussion: no direct lineage or causality.

title: Topological velocity inference from spatial transcriptomic data
concrete_content: TopoVelo extends RNA velocity with spatially coupled differential equations to infer temporal and spatial cell-state dynamics and neighbourhood dependencies.
decision_changed: Creates a separate velocity route requiring kinetic diagnostics and blocks equating arrows with lineage or migration.
constraints: Velocity depends on splicing, kinetics, topology and spatial coupling assumptions and is not direct temporal observation.
skill_action: Audit gene kinetics and fit; compare spatial and non-spatial velocity; perturb neighbourhood choices; seek measured time or lineage validation.
writing_requirement: Methods: count layers, kinetics and spatial graph; Results: fit and directional stability; Figure legend: inferred velocity; Discussion: non-lineage and non-migration boundary.

title: Bridging the dimensional gap from planar spatial transcriptomics to 3D cell atlases
concrete_content: SpatialZ generates virtual sections between sparse measured sections and builds dense single-cell 3D atlases, including a more than 38-million-cell brain atlas.
decision_changed: Requires virtual sections to remain an inferred layer and introduces held-out-section validation for 3D reconstruction.
constraints: Abrupt boundaries, missing tissue and sparse spacing are weakly identifiable; interpolation is not new measurement.
skill_action: Reserve measured slices for blind validation; map uncertainty by distance from measured sections; keep measured and virtual layers separable.
writing_requirement: Methods: section spacing, alignment, model and holdouts; Results: held-out error and uncertainty; Figure legend: measured or virtual slice; Discussion: interpolation and missing-anatomy limits.

title: Inferring allele-specific copy number aberrations and tumor phylogeography from spatially resolved transcriptomics
concrete_content: CalicoST jointly infers allele-specific CNAs, copy-neutral LOH, mirrored subclonal CNAs and spatial tumour phylogeography from SRT, including adjacent-section 3D analyses.
decision_changed: Allows RNA-derived clonal hypotheses only with explicit allelic evidence, tumour-purity sensitivity and orthogonal DNA validation.
constraints: Low RNA coverage, allelic bias and normal-cell admixture affect calls; inferred clones and trees are not measured genomes.
skill_action: Audit informative SNPs and purity; compare total-copy baselines; validate key clones with DNA, FISH or mutation assays.
writing_requirement: Methods: alleles, purity, model and DNA reference; Results: uncertainty and validated events; Figure legend: RNA-inferred CNA or clone; Discussion: phylogeny and DNA boundary.

title: Paired mutation calling and spatial transcriptomics identify cellular neighborhoods associated with the neoplastic outcome of mouse colitis
concrete_content: Combines in vivo lineage tracing, mutation profiling, spatial transcriptomics and modelling to relate clone fates to inflammatory, epithelial and immune neighbourhoods in colitis-associated tumorigenesis.
decision_changed: Demonstrates the evidence ladder needed before linking spatial environment to clone selection and neoplastic outcome.
constraints: Mouse colitis biology may not transfer to human tumours; neighbourhood association alone does not prove selection mechanism.
skill_action: Require mutation or barcode identity plus spatial context; model clone-by-niche alternatives; validate in independent tissue or perturbation.
writing_requirement: Methods: mutation, lineage, neighbourhood and model; Results: clone-niche effect and replication; Figure legend: measured clone versus inferred neighbourhood; Discussion: model-species and causality limits.

title: Simultaneous CRISPR screening and spatial transcriptomics reveal intracellular, intercellular, and functional transcriptional circuits
concrete_content: Perturb-FISH combines in situ guide detection, imaging spatial transcriptomics and functional readouts in monocytes, 3D xenografts and iPSC-derived astrocytes.
decision_changed: Separates directly observed spatial perturbation effects from virtual knockout and enables intracellular, intercellular and density-dependent estimands.
constraints: Effects are model, guide, density and environment specific; screens do not automatically establish human tissue relevance.
skill_action: Audit guide identity, efficiency, off-targets, controls and spatial exposure; model guide-by-neighbourhood effects; validate priority mechanisms.
writing_requirement: Methods: guides, assignment, controls and spatial model; Results: guide effects and interaction terms; Figure legend: perturbed versus predicted; Discussion: context and transfer limits.

modality: lineage tracing plus imaging spatial transcriptomics
title: SpaceBar enables single-cell-resolution clone tracing with imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
concrete_content: Uses 96 synthetic sequences in combinatorial cellular barcodes to pair clone identity with imaging-based spatial gene expression.
decision_changed: Enables explicit separation of clonal inheritance and local-environment association instead of inferring lineage from transcriptomic similarity.
constraints: Barcode collision, dropout, detectability and fitness effects require control; statistical separation does not prove a mechanism.
skill_action: Report barcode design, collision and recovery; test clone-by-location models; retain unassigned cells; validate clone-specific findings.
writing_requirement: Methods: barcode library, assignment and collision control; Results: clone recovery and environmental effects; Figure legend: barcode-observed clone; Discussion: dropout and mechanistic boundary.

title: Cross-species single-cell spatial transcriptomic atlases of the cerebellar cortex
concrete_content: Builds macaque, marmoset and mouse cerebellar spatial atlases and compares cell subtypes, layers, region-selective genes and transcriptomic gradients with functional-connectivity gradients.
decision_changed: Requires orthology, region and sampling audits before calling a spatial feature conserved or species specific.
constraints: Cross-species mapping, technical differences and regional sampling can mimic divergence; fMRI concordance remains correlational.
skill_action: Use one-to-one ortholog and sensitivity sets; model species at the biological-sample level; validate spatial markers in each species.
writing_requirement: Methods: species, regions, orthology and harmonization; Results: conserved and divergent effects; Figure legend: species and mapping; Discussion: sampling, technology and correlation limits.

title: Whole-embryo spatial transcriptomics at subcellular resolution from gastrulation to organogenesis
concrete_content: weMERFISH directly measures 495 genes at subcellular resolution in zebrafish embryos and integrates broader transcriptomic, chromatin-accessibility and live-imaging atlases to study pattern formation.
decision_changed: Forces direct spatial measurements to be separated from integrated atlas values and demonstrates how live imaging can adjudicate competing pattern mechanisms.
constraints: Only 495 genes are directly measured in situ; integrated 25,872-gene expression and chromatin resources are not all direct spatial observations.
skill_action: Maintain modality and measured-feature provenance; validate integrated patterns within the measured panel; distinguish expression change from cell sorting.
writing_requirement: Methods: measured panel and integrated resources; Results: direct versus integrated evidence; Figure legend: modality and measured status; Discussion: targeted-panel and developmental-transfer limits.
